summary: The LLM landscape in late 2026 is dominated by a handful of frontier families from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with strong open-weight competition from Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen. Real-world developer adoption is driven heavily by enterprise aggregator availability (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), where secure cloud access multiplies effective reach far beyond direct API numbers. Because much of the newest research data references models whose exact names cannot be reliably confirmed, this ranking conservatively uses only models with well-established, verifiable naming and documented current availability.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Remains the most widely called general-purpose model across direct API and Azure OpenAI Service, giving it unmatched enterprise aggregator reach.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring multimodal input and reliability

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Shipped February 17 matching Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing, and is available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API, driving heavy enterprise coding adoption.
models.best_for: Enterprise coding assistants and agentic development workflows

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: The context-window king with native Google Vertex AI distribution, giving it strong enterprise reach among Google Cloud customers.
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and multimodal reasoning tasks

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Low-cost, high-throughput variant with a 1M token context widely adopted for high-volume workloads via Vertex AI.
models.best_for: High-volume, cost-sensitive production tasks needing long context

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B MoE reasoning specialist (37B active) and the cheapest frontier-class model, with strong HuggingFace download volume due to open weights.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: Popular open-weight general model with high HuggingFace adoption, offering near-frontier performance at a fraction of proprietary costs.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: One of the most-downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, giving it very broad enterprise reach.
models.best_for: Customizable, self-hosted, and fine-tuned open-model deployments

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Fast, low-cost member of the Claude family widely used for high-throughput tasks and available via Bedrock and Vertex AI.
strengths: Strong instruction following for its size

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's dedicated reasoning model with growing adoption for complex problem-solving, available through direct API and Azure OpenAI.
strengths: Strong on math and coding benchmarks
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, research, and hard coding problems

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading frontier-class model with notable adoption via Azure and AWS Bedrock, favored by EU enterprises for data-residency reasons.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: A large MoE open-weight model with rapidly growing HuggingFace downloads and strong adoption in Asia, clustering closely with Mistral Large 2 in overall reach.
